messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Detected sudden spike in cross-region 5xx and latency originating from eu-west -> us-east (routing anomalies). Automated threshold tripped (p50 latency +180ms, 5xx rate x3 baseline). Paging oncall.
Alex W: I'm on it, looking at the graph. Seeing a step change around 09:03 UTC. Lots of requests for /v1/generate hitting us-east backends from eu-west.
Maya R: I pushed a routing policy change ~08:58 UTC to add a new pin rule for eu-west -> us-east for canary traffic. Could that correlate? :eyes:
Rana S: @Maya R which repo/PR? Can you paste the policy diff?
Maya R: It was https://git.internal/repo/routing/policies PR#492 - added region pin override for region=eu-west -> target=us-east to test cost steering for a small customer cohort.
Chris L: Paging oncall-bot: please confirm who is primary for net infra.
oncall-bot: @Rana S is oncall (pager duty) for eng-sre.
Rana S: I'm oncall, looking at route decisions now. Quick checks:
- `dig` from eu-west edge to model-service.dns -> resolves to us-east LB
- traceroute shows expected path but higher RTTs
- tcpdump shows repeated SYN/RST from mid-route device
Eli T: Any change to DNS TTLs or geo-dns config recently?
Alex W: No TTL changes in last 48h. Only that routing policy PR mentioned. I can pull the policy audit logs.
Maya R: I ran a dry-run before merging but might have missed an overlapping pin rule. Full snippet below:
```
policy "region_pin_euwest_canary" {
  match: src.region == "eu-west" && svc == "model-gen"
  action: pin(target="us-east", weight=0.05)
}
```
incident-bot: deploy-bot: routing-policy updated by maya.r at 08:59:12 UTC (commit 7f9c)
Chris L: That pin looks fine for low weight but maybe the evaluation engine mis-evaluated the overlapping rules and applied full weight. Check policy evaluation logs.
Alex W: Pulling evaluation trace now...
```
EVAL TRACE: request from eu-west user -> matched policy region_pin_euwest_canary (weight resolved = 1.0) -> route to us-east
CONTEXT: overlapping rule region_pin_euwest_global had priority 50, region_pin_euwest_canary priority 40
```
Rana S: Wait priority lower but weight became 1.0 -> suggests a bug in weight normalization when multiple pins exist. Might be a regression from the last scheduler patch.
Maya R: I can roll back the canary rule immediately if you want.
Rana S: Please do. Rollback to last commit before 7f9c. Also temporarily increase TTL and add a high-priority fallback that steers eu-west -> eu-central until we confirm fix.
Maya R: Rolling back now. Reverting commit 7f9c...
deploy-bot: Revert initiated by Maya R at 09:06:22 UTC (revert commit 7f9c -> rollforward 0f3a). Status: in-progress.
Alex W: After the rollback, 5xx rate dropped ~30% in the next minute but still elevated. Some sessions appear stuck with stale KV cache on us-east nodes for long sequences.
Eli T: Could be a KV cache mismatch between model variants across regions - if traffic abruptly shifted, KV warmup causing timeouts. Try soft-fail routing to eu-central for new sessions only.
Rana S: I'm applying a temporary routing override (emergency) with higher priority:
```
override "eu-west-emergency-2026-03-15" {
  match: src.region == "eu-west" && svc == "model-gen"
  action: steer(target="eu-central", priority=100)
}
```
Rana S: Override pushed at 09:08:10 UTC.
incident-bot: routing-control: override created by Rana S id=ovr-20260315-001
Chris L: Confirming traffic now: d/s from eu-west to eu-central increased, us-east traffic down to background levels. p50 latency trending down.
Maya R: Sorry all, this was intended to be a tiny canary. I'll open a postmortem PR to add more test coverage around weight handling.
Alex W: Customer impact: monitoring shows ~12% of requests from eu-west got 502/504 during 09:03-09:12 window. Affected endpoints were some dedicated model endpoints used by a handful of enterprise customers (low volume but high SLA). Alerts from CSM: one customer reported degraded response times.
Rana S: I'm contacting support to notify affected customers and provide status. @Chris L can you craft an incident blurb we can push to status.redwood.ai? Keep it factual: cause = routing policy mis-evaluation, mitigation = override & rollback, ETA next update in 30m.
Chris L: On it.
Chris L: Draft: "We observed a routing policy mis-evaluation causing a portion of eu-west traffic to be routed to us-east, resulting in elevated errors and latency for some model endpoints. We have reverted the recent policy and applied a temporary override to steer traffic to eu-central. We are monitoring and will update in 30 minutes." Thoughts?
Alex W: Good. Add approx impacted % and timeframe. I'll send logs to SRE and CS.
Maya R: Post-rollback, I'm running a quick unit/regression test locally for the scheduler normalization logic. If I can reproduce, I'll open a hotfix PR and we can canary it in eu-central only.
Rana S: Action items:
- Maya: PR + tests for weight normalization (hotfix candidate)
- Alex: Collect eval traces and per-request routing decisions for 09:00-09:15 UTC (forensics)
- Chris: Incident blurb + update status page
- Eli: Verify KV cache warmup health and any lingering 5xx from backend timeouts
- Rana: Keep override until we validate hotfix or until traffic stabilizes
Eli T: Noted. Also will run a small synthetic load from eu-west to confirm steady-state.
incident-bot: Pager cleared for oncall at 09:20 UTC (incident still active, monitoring)
Alex W: Forensics - found a race when overlapping pins exist and one is canary weight <1. Scheduler's union step can accidentally normalize to 1.0 when sum of weights < threshold due to float rounding.
Maya R: I can reproduce locally by creating two overlapping pins with low weights. Fix looks small - clamp weights and add an assertion.
Rana S: If Maya's hotfix is ready, we will canary to eu-central only and then gradually remove override. Don't push to global until we've validated.
Maya R: Opening PR now: https://git.internal/repo/routing/policies/pull/504 - includes test + fix. Requesting review from @Alex W and @Rana S.
Chris L: Status update posted to status page and CS notified. CS reports one enterprise opened a ticket; we assigned a mitigation update.
Alex W: p50 latency back to baseline, 5xx at ~5% above baseline but trending down. Keep monitoring for 30 minutes.
Rana S: Maintaining override. If metrics stable at 10:00 UTC, we'll plan to remove override and apply hotfix in a controlled canary.
Maya R: Thanks everyone. I'll run through the postmortem template after this. :thumbsup:
Eli T: I'll close the synthetic validation once we hit steady-state and push results to the thread.
Rana S: End of current update. Next update in 30m or on any regression. :white_check_mark:
